description:

- /tmp/polygons-gainforest-explore/app/telegram-debug/page.tsx (create)
- /tmp/polygons-gainforest-explore/README.md (modify)

## What to do
Add a minimal, isolated Telegram diagnostics route on the polygons app domain so we can determine whether Telegram injects the Web App API at all for this deployment.

The new route must be independent of the wrapper and draw flows. It should not embed `/draw`, should not depend on polygon state, and should not call `sendData`.

- `window.Telegram`: YES/NO

- current `window.location.href`
- `navigator.userAgent`
- whether the Telegram Web App script tag loaded successfully

- explicitly load `https://telegram.org/js/telegram-web-app.js`
- evaluate the diagnostics on mount and re-check once after a short delay in case Telegram injects late
- keep the page mobile-readable and text-first for screenshots
- document the `/telegram-debug` route in README as a temporary/diagnostic route for Telegram launch troubleshooting

## Don't
- Do not embed the map or iframe on this page
- Do not add backend calls or bot logic here
- Do not remove the existing `/telegram-draw` route or wrapper behavior

title: Harden setup.sh with arch check and swap setup
description:
## Files

## What to do
Add two new checks to setup.sh, inserted AFTER the platform detection section (after line 46) and BEFORE the Node.js check (line 56):

### 1. Architecture gate (between steps 1 and 2)
After detecting PLATFORM and ARCH, add:
```bash
# --------------- 1b. Architecture check (Linux only) ---------------
if [ "$PLATFORM" = "Linux" ]; then
  if [ "$ARCH" != "aarch64" ] && [ "$ARCH" != "x86_64" ]; then
    err "❌ Unsupported architecture: $ARCH"
    err "   Pi-Tainá requires 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (aarch64)."
    err "   32-bit (armv7l/armhf) is not supported."
    err "   Download 64-bit OS: https://www.raspberrypi.com/software/"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$ARCH" = "aarch64" ]; then
    ok "✅ 64-bit ARM detected"
  fi
fi
```

### 2. Swap check for low-RAM systems (Linux only, after arch check)
```bash
# --------------- 1c. RAM/swap check (Linux only) ---------------
if [ "$PLATFORM" = "Linux" ]; then
  TOTAL_MEM_KB=$(grep MemTotal /proc/meminfo | awk '{print $2}')
  TOTAL_MEM_MB=$((TOTAL_MEM_KB / 1024))
  if [ "$TOTAL_MEM_MB" -lt 1500 ]; then
    SWAP_KB=$(grep SwapTotal /proc/meminfo | awk '{print $2}')
    SWAP_MB=$((SWAP_KB / 1024))
    if [ "$SWAP_MB" -lt 1024 ]; then
      warn "⚠️  Low RAM (${TOTAL_MEM_MB}MB) and swap (${SWAP_MB}MB) detected."
      warn "   npm install may fail. Consider adding swap:"
      info "     sudo dphys-swapfile swapoff"
      info "     sudo sed -i 's/CONF_SWAPSIZE=.*/CONF_SWAPSIZE=2048/' /etc/dphys-swapfile"
      info "     sudo dphys-swapfile setup && sudo dphys-swapfile swapon"
      echo ""
      warn "Continue anyway? [y/N]"
      if [ "$HAS_TTY" = true ]; then
        read -r SWAP_ANSWER < /dev/tty || SWAP_ANSWER="n"
      else
        SWAP_ANSWER="y"
      fi
      case "$SWAP_ANSWER" in
        [yY]|[yY][eE][sS]) info "Continuing..." ;;
        *) err "Setup aborted. Add swap and re-run."; exit 1 ;;
      esac
    else
      ok "✅ Sufficient swap (${SWAP_MB}MB)"
    fi
  fi
fi
```

### 3. Also add git check at the very beginning (before Node.js)
```bash
# --------------- 1d. Check git ---------------
if ! command -v git &>/dev/null; then
  if [ "$PLATFORM" = "Linux" ]; then
    warn "⚠️  git not found — installing..."
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git
  else
    err "❌ git is required. Install it and re-run."
    exit 1
  fi
fi
```

## Don't
- Don't change the existing Node.js, Python, npm install, .env, or pm2 sections
- Don't change the color helpers or banner
- Don't add Docker or container logic
- Don't make the script non-idempotent — all new checks must be safe to run multiple times

3. setup.sh installs git on Linux if missing
4. All existing setup.sh functionality is preserved (Node, Python, npm, .env, pm2)
5. Script remains idempotent — running twice produces no errors

title: Create setup.sh — cross-platform setup script for macOS and Raspberry Pi
description:

## What to do
Create a single setup script that handles the full first-run experience on both macOS (Apple Silicon) and Raspberry Pi OS (ARM64 Debian). The script should be idempotent — safe to run multiple times.

### Script structure

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
```

### 1. Platform detection
```bash
OS="$(uname -s)"   # Darwin or Linux
ARCH="$(uname -m)" # arm64 or aarch64 or x86_64
```
Print a banner: '🌿 Pi-Tainá Setup' and detected platform.

### 2. Check/install Node.js 20+
- If `node` exists and version >= 20, print '✅ Node.js vX.Y.Z' and skip
- If `node` is missing or < 20:
  - **macOS**: check if `brew` exists. If yes: `brew install node@20`. If no brew: print instructions to install Homebrew first, then exit 1.
  - **Linux (RPi)**: use NodeSource setup:
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash -
    sudo apt-get install -y nodejs
    ```
- After install, verify `node --version` >= 20 or exit 1

### 3. Check/install Python 3
- If `python3` exists, print '✅ Python 3.x.x' and skip
- If missing:
  - **macOS**: `brew install python3`
  - **Linux**: `sudo apt-get install -y python3`

### 4. Install npm dependencies
```bash
echo '📦 Installing dependencies...'
npm install
```

### 5. Setup .env file
- If `.env` already exists, print '✅ .env already exists — skipping' and skip
- If `.env` does NOT exist:
  - Copy `.env.example` to `.env`
  - Print a message explaining the 3 required vars:
    ```
    📝 Created .env from template. You need to set these 3 values:

    1. TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — get from @BotFather on Telegram
    2. GEMINI_API_KEY     — get from https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
    3. ADMIN_USER_ID      — get from @userinfobot on Telegram

    Edit .env with: nano .env
    ```

### 6. Optional: install pm2 for service mode
- Ask: 'Install pm2 for always-on service mode? (recommended for Mac Mini / RPi) [y/N]'
- If yes: `npm install -g pm2`
- If no: skip

### 7. Print final instructions
```
🌿 Setup complete!

  Start the bot:     npm start
  Development mode:  npm run dev
  Run smoke test:    npm run test:smoke

  For always-on service:
    pm2 start npm --name taina -- start
    pm2 startup && pm2 save
```

### Style guidelines
- Use emoji for visual clarity (✅ ❌ 📦 🌿 📝)
- Use color via tput if available (green for success, red for errors, yellow for warnings)
- Every step should print what it's doing BEFORE doing it
- If any step fails, print a clear error message and exit 1
- The script should be runnable with `bash setup.sh` (no need for chmod first, though the file should be chmod +x)

## Don't
- Don't use `sudo` on macOS (Homebrew doesn't need it)
- Don't install Docker or any containerization tools
- Don't modify any source code files
- Don't hardcode paths — use relative paths from the script's directory
- Don't ask interactive questions except the pm2 one — everything else should be automatic
- Don't install global npm packages other than pm2 (and only if user says yes)
- Don't assume the user has git (they already cloned, so they do, but don't use git commands)

5. Python3 check: skips if present, installs via brew/apt if missing

```typescript
const incoming: IncomingMessage = {
  chatId: msg.chat.id,
  messageId: msg.message_id,
  text: `The user tapped the "${persistentAction}" quick-action button. They want to ${intentDescription}. Guide them on what to provide next (photo, location, etc).`,
  user,
  isGroup,
  isMentioned: false,
  isAdmin: isAdmin(user.id),
};
await onMessage(incoming);
```

```typescript
const displayName = `${from.first_name} ${from.last_name ?? ""}`.trim();

  text: `The user tapped the "${buttonLabel}" quick-action button. They want to ${intentDescription}. Guide them on what to provide next.`,
```

## What to do
Create a module that manages a local JSON whitelist file for access control.

### Data structure
```ts
export type Role = 'admin' | 'member';

export interface WhitelistEntry {
  userId: number;        // Telegram user ID
  role: Role;
  addedBy: number;       // Telegram user ID of who added them
  addedAt: string;       // ISO 8601 timestamp
  displayName?: string;  // optional, for human readability
}

export interface JoinRequest {
  userId: number;
  displayName: string;
  username?: string;
  requestedAt: string;   // ISO 8601
}

interface WhitelistData {
  entries: WhitelistEntry[];
  pendingRequests: JoinRequest[];
}
```

### File location
`data/whitelist.json` — same directory as sessions. Create `data/` dir if it doesn't exist (use `mkdirSync` with `recursive: true`).

### Exported functions

1. **`initWhitelist(adminUserId: number): void`**
   - Load whitelist from disk if exists
   - If file doesn't exist OR the adminUserId is not in entries, ensure adminUserId is in entries with role 'admin', addedBy: adminUserId, addedAt: now
   - Cache in module-level variable

2. **`getRole(userId: number): Role | null`**
   - Return the role of the user, or null if not whitelisted
   - Reads from in-memory cache (loaded at init)

3. **`isAuthorized(userId: number): boolean`**
   - Returns true if user has any role (admin or member)

4. **`isAdmin(userId: number): boolean`**
   - Returns true if user role is 'admin'

5. **`addMember(userId: number, addedBy: number, displayName?: string): boolean`**
   - Add user as 'member'. If already exists, return false. Save to disk. Return true.

6. **`removeMember(userId: number): boolean`**
   - Remove user from entries. Cannot remove admins (return false). Save to disk. Return true if removed.

7. **`addJoinRequest(userId: number, displayName: string, username?: string): boolean`**
   - Add to pendingRequests if not already there and not already a member. Save to disk. Return true if added.

8. **`getPendingRequests(): JoinRequest[]`**
   - Return copy of pendingRequests array.

9. **`approveRequest(userId: number, approvedBy: number): boolean`**
   - Move user from pendingRequests to entries as 'member'. Save to disk. Return true if found and moved.

10. **`denyRequest(userId: number): boolean`**
    - Remove from pendingRequests. Save to disk. Return true if found.

11. **`getMembers(): WhitelistEntry[]`**
    - Return copy of entries array.

### File I/O
- Use `fs.readFileSync` / `fs.writeFileSync` (synchronous is fine for a small JSON file)
- Write with `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)` for readability
- Wrap reads in try/catch — if file is corrupt, log warning and start fresh with just the admin

### Constants
```ts

```

## Don't
- Don't use any database or external service
- Don't use async file I/O (keep it simple, file is tiny)
- Don't export the WhitelistData type (internal)
- Don't add any Telegram-specific logic (this module is pure data)

title: Epic: Local-first access control & tool sandboxing
description:
## Why
The Pi agent exposes bash, read, edit, write tools to ALL Telegram users by default. Any stranger who discovers the bot can: read .env (steal all API keys), execute arbitrary shell commands, modify bot code, publish fake records under the community identity, and exhaust paid API quotas. This is a critical security vulnerability for a bot designed to run on community hardware.

## What success looks like
- Only whitelisted Telegram user IDs can interact with the bot
- Members get custom tools only (identify, publish, forest report, etc.) — NO filesystem/bash access
- Admins get full tool access (for skill building and maintenance)
- Unknown users get a friendly rejection message and can request access
- Admins can approve/remove members via Telegram commands
- All access control is local-first: a JSON file on disk, no external database
- The whitelist file lives in data/whitelist.json, gitignored, persists across restarts

## Key constraints
- No external auth services (no Supabase, no OAuth, no cloud)
- No breaking changes to existing tool signatures
- Whitelist must survive bot restarts (file-based persistence)
- First admin bootstrapped via ADMIN_USER_ID env var
- Must work in both DM and group chat contexts
- Friendly Tainá-personality responses for unauthorized users

description:
## Files
- skills/organization-setup/SKILL.md (create)

## What to do

Create the skill file that teaches Tainá how to guide users through creating an organization. Follow the format of skills/hypercerts/SKILL.md exactly (frontmatter + markdown).

### Frontmatter
```yaml
---
name: organization-setup
description: Create a new organization on the climateai.org network. Use when users want to set up their community, NGO, or conservation project as an organization. Tainá guides them through a natural conversation, extracting info from voice notes and messages.
---
```

### Content must cover

**When to Use:**
- User says "set up our organization", "create an org", "register our community", "I want to create an account for our project"
- User asks how to publish data under their own name/org
- User mentions they want their own climateai.org handle

**When NOT to Use:**
- User wants to identify a species → identify_species
- User wants to create a bumicert → create_hypercert
- User wants to publish an observation → publish_occurrence

**Core principles (write these as instructions to Tainá):**

1. EXTRACT, DONT INTERROGATE — If a user sends a voice note or long message, extract every field you can (name, type, location, founded date, description, member info). Then only ask about what is still missing. Never re-ask for info already provided.

2. VOICE NOTES ARE FIRST-CLASS — Open with "Tell me about your organization — you can type or send me a voice note 🎤". A single voice note can fill 5+ fields. Use transcribe_voice, then parse the transcription for org name, type, location, year, description, member details.

3. INFER AND CONFIRM — If they mention "Costa Rica" → set country without asking. If they say "nonprofit" in passing → set type. If their Telegram name is "María García" → suggest as member name. Never ask for what you already know.

4. IMAGES ARE NATURAL — "Send me a photo that represents your org — your logo, your team, your land 📸". If they send a square/small image → avatar. If wide/landscape → banner. Invite images, dont demand them.

5. ONE QUESTION AT A TIME — Never dump multiple questions. Ask one thing, wait for the answer, then ask the next.

6. SKIP IS ALWAYS OK — User can say "skip" or "thats all" at any point. Only 4 fields are truly required: displayName, handle, organizationType, description. Everything else is optional.

**The flow (write as numbered steps):**

1. User triggers org creation intent
2. Tainá opens warmly: "Lets do it! Tell me about your organization — whats it called and what do you do? You can type or send me a voice note 🎤"
3. Parse response — extract everything possible (name, type, location, year, description, member info)
4. Celebrate what they do: "Thats amazing work!" / "Love it!" — be genuine
5. Suggest a handle based on the name (lowercase, hyphens, max 20 chars): "How about cabarete-sostenible.climateai.org?"
6. Ask about missing REQUIRED fields only (type if not mentioned, description if too short)
7. Naturally weave in optional fields: "Do you have a website or social media?" / "Send me your logo 📸" / "What year were you founded?"
8. Ask about first member: "Should I add you as the first member? Whats your name and role?"
9. Show confirmation summary using this format:
   📛 Name
   🔗 handle.climateai.org
   🏷️ Types
   📝 Description (truncated)
   📍 Location (if provided)
   🌐 Website (if provided)
   📱 Social links (if provided)
   📅 Founded (if provided)
   🎯 Goals (if provided)
   🖼️ Logo/banner (if provided)
   👤 Member — Role (if provided)
   
   "Ready to create? 🌿"
10. On confirmation → call create_organization with all collected fields
11. Celebrate: "Your organization is live! 🎉 🔗 handle.climateai.org"
12. Offer next step: "Want to start recording observations? 📸" or "Want to create a bumicert for your project?"

**Handle generation rules:**
- Lowercase the org name
- Replace spaces with hyphens
- Remove special characters
- Truncate to 20 chars max (climateai.org has limits)
- If truncated, try to cut at a word boundary

**Dont section:**
- Dont ask numbered questions or follow a rigid script
- Dont ask for info already provided (even in passing, even from voice notes)
- Dont ask more than one question at a time
- Dont require optional fields
- Dont expose the password in Telegram messages
- Dont create without showing summary and getting confirmation
- Dont say "Question 3:" or "Step 2:" — this is a conversation
- Dont ask "What is your organization type?" if they already said "were a nonprofit"
- Dont skip the confirmation summary — always show it before creating
- Dont forget to celebrate their work — these are real communities doing real conservation
acceptance_criteria:
1. File skills/organization-setup/SKILL.md exists
2. Has correct frontmatter with name: organization-setup and description
3. Includes When to Use and When NOT to Use sections
4. Documents all 5 core principles: extract dont interrogate, voice notes first-class, infer and confirm, images natural, one question at a time
5. Documents the full conversational flow (12 steps)
6. Documents handle generation rules
7. Documents the confirmation summary format with emoji
8. Has a Dont section with at least 8 prohibitions
9. Follows the same markdown structure as skills/hypercerts/SKILL.md

- Cause: Not enough RAM + swap
- Fix: Add swap (link to the swap instructions in the RPi requirements section added by task .1)

- Cause: Running 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS

- Cause: Missing .env variables


```
GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude={lat}&longitude={lng}&current=temperature_2m,relative_humidity_2m,apparent_temperature,precipitation,weather_code,wind_speed_10m,wind_direction_10m,is_day&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,precipitation_probability_max,wind_speed_10m_max,weather_code,sunrise,sunset&timezone=auto&forecast_days=3
```

- 0: Clear sky → ☀️ (day) / 🌙 (night)

YAML frontmatter:
```yaml
---
name: hypercerts
description: Create hypercerts (impact certificates) to document conservation projects, community initiatives, and environmental work. Use when users want to record project-level impact — not individual species observations.
---
```

Content sections:

**## When to Use**
- User talks about a project, initiative, or campaign (not a single species sighting)
- User mentions reforestation, cleanup, monitoring program, community garden, etc.
- User explicitly asks to create a hypercert or impact certificate
- User wants to document ongoing or completed conservation work

**## When NOT to Use**
- User sends a photo of a species → use identify_species + publish_occurrence instead
- User asks about forest health → use forest_report instead
- User just wants to search existing records → use query_hyperindex instead

**## How to Use**
1. Gather the basics: what was the project? (title + short description)
2. Ask about timeframe: when did it start? Is it ongoing or finished?
3. Ask about location: where did this happen? (use geocode_location if needed)
4. If the user sent a photo, it will be attached automatically
5. Suggest work scope tags based on what they described
6. Call create_hypercert with all gathered info
7. Share the Hyperscan link so they can view their impact certificate

**## Presentation**
- Celebrate the creation: 'Your impact is now on the record! 🏆'
- Share the Hyperscan URL so they can view and share it
- Explain briefly: 'A hypercert is like a certificate for your conservation work — it's permanent and verifiable'
- Don't overwhelm with technical details about ATProto or DIDs

**## Don't**
- Don't create a hypercert for every species observation — those are occurrences
- Don't require all fields — title and short description are enough
- Don't ask more than 2 questions before creating — gather what you can and fill in defaults

### skills/hyperindex/SKILL.md

Create a behavioral guide for querying the Hypersphere network.

YAML frontmatter:
```yaml
---
name: hyperindex
description: Search and browse biodiversity records and hypercerts on the Hypersphere network. Use when users ask about existing observations, want to see community records, or search for species data.
---
```

Content sections:

**## When to Use**
- User asks 'what have we recorded?' or 'show me our observations'
- User asks about a specific species across the network
- User wants to see hypercerts or impact certificates
- User asks 'how many records do we have?'

**## How to Use**
- For community records: use type='occurrences' or type='hypercerts' with the community DID
- For species search: use type='search' with the species name
- For browsing: use type='occurrences' without a DID filter to see recent records from everyone
- Keep limit reasonable (5-10 for display, up to 20 for counts)

**## Presentation**
- Summarize results naturally: 'We've recorded 23 species so far! Here are the most recent...'
- For occurrences: show species name, location, date
- For hypercerts: show title, description, date
- Always include the Hyperscan link for records the user might want to explore
- If no results: 'No records found yet — want to be the first to contribute?'

**## Don't**
- Don't dump raw JSON or URIs on the user
- Don't show DIDs — they're internal identifiers
- Don't show more than 5 records at a time unless asked
- Don't query without a purpose — always in response to a user question

## Don't
- Don't add code examples to skill files
- Don't reference internal file paths or implementation details
- Don't make the skills longer than ~40 lines each
